summary.headline: Consolidated total income rose 61% YoY to INR 16,746 million in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA up 29% to INR 3,004 million, though margin fell to 17.9%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated total income grew 61% YoY to INR 16,746 million and EBITDA rose 29% to INR 3,004 million, with H1 total income at INR 31,738 million (up 56%). Growth was helped by the three Antolin India entities acquired recently, while standalone total income grew 17% YoY to INR 10,500 million. EBITDA margin was 17.9%, hit by commodity and direct material costs, a sales mix shift toward OEM and minimum wage revisions, with management calling much of this timing-related. Finance costs of INR 234 million in Q2 (INR 486 million in H1) from acquisition debt weighed on PBT, which management says would have grown 23% in Q2 excluding it. A QIP of INR 10,000 million was completed in late August.

segments.name: Standalone powertrain components (pistons, pins, rings, valves)
segments.commentary: Total income up 17% YoY to INR 10,500 million in Q2, in line with the weighted industry production growth of about 17%. Standalone EBITDA margin was 19.9% per management, versus about 21% earlier, as mix shifted toward OEM.

segments.name: High-precision injection molded components
segments.commentary: Gaining from ABS-related demand for 2-wheelers. New Neemrana plant to supply by April, as customers need parts in place by then.

segments.name: EV motors and controllers (TGPEL, Coimbatore)
segments.commentary: Scaling through new Coimbatore facility and a growing customer base. TGPEL capex is ongoing; no figures disclosed.

segments.name: Automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin India, 3 entities)
segments.commentary: Acquired entities are delivering strong operational and financial performance and new customer wins. Lighting is growing faster than the rest of interiors and was close to 20% of interiors revenue at acquisition. Headliner speakerless acoustic technology is at proof-of-concept with 2-3 customers.

guidance_outlook: Management expects piston growth to moderate to a 7-8% CAGR over the next two years, not the 17-20% seen in FY27, citing the high base.
New business wins are expected to add over INR 1,000 crore of mature-year revenue, on top of the existing base of about INR 6,000 crore.
Management expects finance costs to normalise as debt is repaid, with some improvement expected from Q3 FY27.
Management expects to grow in line with or ahead of end markets; it does not give capex figures.
Management is not planning to raise further debt or equity now, but is evaluating acquisitions.
Commodity pass-through lags by about one quarter; a fall in aluminium prices may not add much to margins.
capex_capacity: Capacity additions are under way at Pithampur, Pathredi (recently expanded), Ghaziabad (precision injection molding), a new plant next to the existing Neemrana facility, TGPEL, and Antolin interiors.
Management declined to give an FY27 capex figure, calling it 'very sizable' and subject to change with ongoing decisions.
Capacity is being added ahead of demand; management says there should be no capacity constraint going forward.
Raw material is held for at least 3 months of production in precision plastics, which weighs on working capital.
demand_pricing: Domestic auto production rose about 17% on a weighted-average basis; PV, CV, 2W and 3W all posted record Q2 sales.
Standalone capacity utilisation is around 75-80%, and an OEM surge forced a shift in mix away from aftermarket and exports.
Raw material costs (aluminium, copper, steel, plastics, tools and oils) are passed through to customers with about a one-quarter lag, with recovery described as near 100%.
Gross margin fell to around 55-56% from about 60%. Management could not split the decline between mix and timing lag.
Management expects EV penetration to rise from about 9-10% to 15-16% by 2030, while ICE demand continues.
Headliner content per vehicle is 15-18% higher for small cars and 30-40% higher for larger vehicles (management's estimate).

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex plans, and why did trade payables fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no capex figure, calling it 'very sizable'. Working capital is described as normal across the group, and raw material stock of at least 3 months was held in precision plastics.

qa_highlights.question: Can 10-12% piston growth be sustained over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth would moderate to a 7-8% CAGR in the next two years because of the high FY27 base, and that it does not expect 17-20% to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RM impact in Q2 and the outlook for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RM costs are fully passed through on a one-quarter lag. Aluminium prices are falling, but oil- and tool-linked costs are rising, so the net Q3 effect depends on the war.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone EBITDA margin stay around 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone margin was 19.9% in Q2, near 20% and among the best in the industry, and that the 1-2 point drop was mainly mix.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise debt or equity for acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no debt or equity raise is planned now, the balance sheet is strong, and acquisitions are being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company keep growing after Antolin is consolidated in the base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to outgrow end markets, with growth depending on wins and mix, including lighting and complete-assembly interiors modules.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a defence or aerospace opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees defence as the focus, supplying Shaktiman trucks and the Avadi vehicle factory, but volumes are limited. Aerospace needs 3-5 years of qualification and is not the focus.

risks_watch: Gross margin trend (about 55-56%) and whether the mix and time-lag effects reverse.
Middle East war effects on oil, tool and direct material costs, which are not yet recovered.
Finance cost normalisation in Q3 FY27 as acquisition debt is repaid.
Capacity build-out (Neemrana precision plastics, Ghaziabad, Pithampur, TGPEL, Antolin) and execution.
Minimum wage and gratuity impact on employee costs, with management saying it is fully absorbed.
Piston growth moderating to 7-8% after the FY27 high base.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and volumes, with a cautious note on margins and commodity exposure. Management was evasive on specific capex, order-win details and the split of margin decline between mix and timing lag.
key_quotes: Commodity movements are usually passed through to our customers under back-to-back arrangements with a lag of about a quarter.
So I expect that the next 2 years will get more or less toned down to the CAGR to achieve a total CAGR of around 7% to 8%.

We are putting capacities almost in all the areas, including our legacy business because even with the legacy business, we see that with a 7% or 8% market growth and kind of penetration that we have in the electric segment, we will still require more ICE engines in 2030 and 2032.

growth.why: Management guides piston/standalone growth down to a 7-8% CAGR over the next two years from 17-20%, with over INR 1,000 crore of mature-year wins on a ~INR 6,000 crore base; capacity is being added ahead of demand at several plants, but no capex figures or specific timelines beyond Neemrana by April were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 17.9% from a gross margin of about 60% down to 55-56%, with management calling part of it timing-related and finance costs expected to normalise from Q3 FY27, but the mix and lag split was not disclosed and Middle East war costs are not yet recovered.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Neemrana precision plastics plant is due to supply by April and capacity additions are under way at Pithampur, Pathredi, Ghaziabad, TGPEL and Antolin, with management saying capacity is being added ahead of demand.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone volumes grew about 17% in Q2 in line with industry, but management guides piston growth down to a 7-8% CAGR over the next two years from 17-20%, with capacity utilisation at 75-80%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management calls FY27 capex 'very sizable' and says it is putting a lot into TGPEL, with utilisation at 75-80% and capacity being added ahead of demand, though no figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management has toned down its growth outlook to a 7-8% standalone CAGR from 17-20%, citing the high FY27 base, so the call points away from a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Standalone growth is guided down to 7-8% CAGR and margins may stay pressured by commodity timing and oil/tool costs from the Middle East war, while the Q3 net commodity effect is uncertain.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Headliner speakerless acoustic technology is only at proof-of-concept with 2-3 customers, and lighting and complete-assembly interiors modules are being pursued, but no launch date was given.

rows.label: Over INR 1,000 crore mature-year wins on ~INR 6,000 crore base
rows.why: Management says new business wins should add over INR 1,000 crore of mature-year revenue, about 17% on the existing ~INR 6,000 crore base, though order details were evasive.

rows.label: Finance cost normalisation as acquisition debt is repaid
rows.why: Finance costs were INR 234 million in Q2 and INR 486 million in H1 from Antolin acquisition debt, and management expects improvement from Q3 FY27 with no new debt planned.

rows.label: Defence supply (Shaktiman trucks, Avadi vehicle factory)
rows.why: Defence is the stated focus with supply to Shaktiman and Avadi, but management says volumes are limited, and aerospace needs 3-5 years of qualification.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, industry-linked growth and capacity additions, and cautious on margins, commodity timing and the 1-2 point margin drop; analysts pushed on capex size, payables decline and whether growth holds after the FY27 base.
